2. In Civil Appeal No. 171 of 2000 facts, in brief, are that the respondent Nos. 1-4 and 6-48 along with CCCG, the respondent No. 5, filed Matter No. 6 of 1996 seeking declaration that the issuance of 13790 debentures, each valuing Tk. 10,000/, issued by the company in favour of the appellant No. 1 with 13.5% interest as well as the trust deed in respect thereof being void are liable to be Cancelled on the averments That they, holding 1,29.729 shares, represent 10.50% share hold of the company; the factory of the above company was established at Chittagong in the year 1969 and the company was incorporated in the year 1979; in the year 1989 the appellants, while holding 100% shares of the company, sold their 49% of the shareholding in the company, 34% shares to the members of the public who are represented by the respondent Nos. 1-3 and 15% to its officers and workers who are represented by the respondent No. 4, before the above sale, the company issued prospectus dated 14.2.1989, wherein a sum of Tk. 7,21,34,931/-was shown as quasi-equity loan to the company from the appellant No. 1 with no mention of interest to be charged thereon; however in the balance sheet of the company, as of 30.6.92, Tk. 12,26,56,225 was shown as quasi-equity loan and in the balance sheet there was also no mention of interest on the said quasi equity loan; thereafter the appellants, by agreement S for sale dated 27.6.1993 sold their remaining 51% shares to T.K. Oil Refinery Ltd, the respondent No. 49, and before the sale of the above 51% shares on 27.6.1993 the appellants, holding 51% shares, had five directors in the Board of the Company and the purchasers who bought 49% shares had four directors; the respondent No. 49, after purchasing the balance 51% shares on 27.6.93, similarly had five directors and the purchasers who bought 49% shareholding also had four directors in the Board; the appellants, by virtue. of their majority in the Board of Directors, while selling the balance 51% shares, passed a resolution on 27.6.1992 for issuing 13790 debentures of Tk. 10,000/- each, payable with 13.5% and then the aforesaid debentures were issued and a trust deed was also created in respect of the said debentures and the respondent Nos. 50-54 were made trustees of the said trust deed and in that process a sum of Tk. 33,00,000/- was spent from the fund of the company although there . was no need to form a Board of Trustees as the said debentures were payable only to the appellant No. 1 and accordingly the appellants liable to pay back the said amount of Tk. 33,00,000/-to the company; while I3CIC, the appellant No. 2, took management of the company from 1982, the company started, incurring loss and upto  30.6.1988 the company incurred loss of Tk. 5,4616,579/- but the above loss was not deducted while fixing the amount of the quasi equity loan on the basis of profit made due to revaluation of the assets of the company; the appellants did not give any loan to the company to the tune of the amount as shown as quasi-equity loan and as such they were not entitled to any reimbursement for the said amount against the so called quasi equity roan and as such the issuance of the debentures is void. 

 3. The appellant's contested the above matter and filed affidavit-in-opposition contending that after the management of the company was placed with appellant No. 2 in the year 1982 it made a profit of Tk. 53.74 lacs in the year 1983-84, Tk. 74.52 lacs in the year 1985-86, Tk. 255.97 lacs in the year 1986-87, Tk. 832.90 lacs in 1987-88, Tk. 950.20 lacs in 1988-89, Tk. 771.07 lacs in 1989-90 and Tk. 741.30 lacs in 1990-91 and Tk. 774.10 lacs in 1991-92 and the company declared dividends of 20%, 30%, 35% and 40% in 1988-89, 189-90, 1990-91 and 1991-92 respectively; the appellant No. 1, before selling its 49% of shareholding, decided to make fresh valuation of the assets of the company as since its incorporation the value of the land, building, machinery and other movable and immovable’s of the company including the goodwill increased manifold and on revaluation Tk. 12,26,36,225.00 was found as the appreciated value but however since the company remained under its management and control, the appellant No. 1, without realizing the about amount of Tk. 12,26,36,225.00, allowed the said amount to be retained by the company in the form of quasi-equity loan and also did not charge any interest thereon till sale of the balance 51% shares and at the time of selling the balance 51% shares specifically claimed the above quasi equity loan with interest @ 13.5%; the value of the assets of the company having increased manifold and the company also earned profit of crores of Taka, the value of the shares of the company also increased manifold but the above 49% shares of the company were sold only at face value and so the purchasers of 49% shares to make huge gain, did not raise any objection to the creation of the said quasi equity loan; further the above 49% shares offered to the public was oversubscribed; at the time of transfer of the company to the respondent No. 49 on 27.6.92 by way of selling 51% shares to him, the company owed Tk. 12,26,36,255.00 to the appellant No. 1 against quasi equity loan and there was also an outstanding ADP loan amounting to Tk.1,27,05,450.00 and unpaid foreign loan of Tk. 25,65,030/- total being Tk. 13,79,06,705.00, and accordingly, before the above transfer, the company as per the decision of the Board of Directors, out of the above amount of Tk. 13,79,06,705.00, decided to pay the appellant No. 1 Tk. 6,705.00 in cash and issue in favour of the appellant No. 1, 13.790 debentures of Tk. 10,000.00 each, payable in 20 installments over a period of 10 years with an interest @ 13.50% per year and the respondent No. 49 also considering that the actual value of assets of the company increased manifold and the company was also a profitable concern, apart from purchasing 51% shareholding of the company, that is 4,38,666 shares, at a price of Tk. 33,50,00,000.00, which is many times more then the face value at which minority shareholders purchased 49% shareholding, also agreed to the specific term provided in the public notice issued for sale of 51% shares of the company to the effect that the company will issue 13,790 debentures of Tk. 10,000 each with interest of 13.5% which term, later on, was also incorporated in the agreement for sale dated 27.6.1993; accordingly the application under section 233 is barred hit by the principles of estoppel, acquiescence and waiver. The respondent Nos. 1- 4, who along with respondent Nos.  6-48 and others purchased 49% shares of the company in the year 1989 only at face value and at the time of their purchase did not raise any objection to the creation of quasi equity loan of Tk. 12,26,36,255 as shown in the Balance sheet as on 31.12.1988, in collusion with each other, also filed Title Suit No. 207 of 1993 for the selfsame relief as sought in the application filed under section 233 of the Companies Act and the said suit being still pending, the present application is also not maintainable. 

 4. In Civil Appeal No. 172 of 2000 facts, in brief, are that the respondent Nos. 1-5 of the above appeal similarly filed Matter No. 22 of 1997 praying for cancellation of Debenture Nos. 1-10350 issued in favour of the appellant No. 1 and Debenture Nos.  10351-28250 issued in favour of the appellant No. 2 and also for cancellation of the resolutions dated 22.4.93 and 10.5.93 passed by the Board of Directors and also the resolutions dated 28.2.93 and 11.4.93 passed in the extra ordinary general meeting of the company regarding issue of the above debentures on the averments that they represent 10% shareholding of the above company; the appellant No. 1, while owning 100% shareholding of the above company and managing the affairs of the company through the appellant No. 2, deciding to sell its 49% shareholding issued prospectus wherein the net worth of the above company, as per revaluation made as on 31.3.1988, was shown at Tk. 15,27,99,818.00, being interest free quasi equity loan of Tk. 10,27,99,818.00 to the company from the appellant No. 1 and Tk. 5,00,00,000.00 being the paid up capital to be subscribed in total including off-loading; the term "quasi-equity loan" apparently means that the appellant No. 1 has given the amount shown as quasi equity loan to the company which is an asset of the company and any investor will take it to be so but later on it was revealed by the appellants that this was actually a liability of the company and the above amount of Tk. 10,27,99,818.00 belonged to them and the respondents came to know that the appellants, who had the absolute majority and control over the affairs of the company at the time of disinvestment of 49% shareholding in the year 1988, decided to expropriate Tk. 10,35,07,245.00, the appreciated value of the assets of the company after revaluation, by showing the same as "quasi-equity loan" in the prospectus dated 31.12.1988; in the balance sheet of the company dated 31.8.1988 for the  years 1987-1988 the above quasi equity loan was not shown; the decision to pay the quasi-equity loan by the company to the appellant No. 1 was taken without any Board Resolution in 1988; the Auditor's Report to the Balance Sheet for the year ending 30.06.89, 3.6.90, 30.6.91, 30.6.92 and 30.6.93 also showed the said sum of Tk. 10,35,07,274 as interest free quasi equity loan; in the year 1993 the appellant No. 1, who earlier in the year 1988 already sold 49% shareholding i.e 2,45,00 shares, decided to sell the balance 51% shareholding, i.e 2,55,000 shares, and for that purpose by public notice dated 15.11.92 invited tenders for sale of the shares and the terms and conditions of the above sale were contained in the said public notice to the effect the buyer will acknowledge that the company will issue debentures with interest against the quasi equity loan and the highest bid of Mr. Obaidul Karim, the respondent No. 2, for Tk. 7,97 crores being accepted, the above 255,000 were sold to him by agreement of sale deed dated 3.8.1993 and in the said agreement the respondent No. 2 also agreed that the company will pay the above quasi-equity loan to the appellant No. 1 by issuing 10350 of debentures of Tk. 10,000 each, with interest (a) 13.5% and thereby the company was saddled with the above liability of quasi-equity loan with interest @ 13.5%; the appellants, by dint of their majority shareholding, by resolution dated 22.4.93, 12.5.93 passed by the Board and by resolutions dated 28.2.93 and 11.4.93 passed in the extraordinary general meeting of the company, got the issuance of the above 10350 secured redeemable debentures of Tk. 10,000 each, bearing interest at 13.5% repayable within 10 years in favour of the appellant No. 1 and also, against the entire dues of the appellant No. 2, got issuance of 17900 secured redeemable debentures bearing interest at 13.5% repayable within 10 years which are against the interest Of the shareholders as well as the company. 

 5. The appellant No. 2 contested the above matter and filed affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that before issuing the prospectus for 49% shareholding, the value of the assets of the company was revalued by the Charted Accountants on 31.3.1988 because since its incorporation the value of the assets of the company increased manifold and after revaluation, the appreciated value, i.e Tk. 10,35,07,274.00, was shown as "quasi-equity loan" given to the company by the appellant No. 1; in the prospectus issued on 10.5.1988 the above amount of Tk. 10,35,07,274.00 being shown as quasi equity loan, the purchasers of the 49% shareholding including  the respondent Nos. 1-5 had knowledge of the said quasi equity loan and they purchased 49% shares of the company without raising any objection to the creation of above quasi 'equity loan as those 49% shares were sold to them only at face value though the actual value of shares of the company was much more as the actual value of the assets having increased manifold and the company was also a profitable concern; so the respondent Nos. 1-5 having purchased the shares only at face value and without raising any objection to the creation of quasi equity loan, are not entitled to get any relief in view of the principles of waiver, acquisance and estopped; further the appellant No. 1, on consideration that till sale of the balance 51% shareholding the company would remain under its management, did not realize the said quasi equity loan at the time of sale of 49% shares and also did not demand only interest on the said amount and interest was demanded on the same subsequently while the debentures were issued after sale of balance 51% shares. 

 6. In Civil Appeal No. 173 of 2000 facts, in brief, are that the sole respondent similarly filed Matter No. 47 of 1996 praying for cancellation of the resolutions of the Board of Directors passed in the 74th and 76th of meetings of the Board approving quasi equity loan of Tk. 5,25,33,742.00 and the issuance of Debenture Nos.  01-5253 and 5254-1203 on the averments that he represents more than 10% of share-holding of the company; the appellant No. 1 in the year 1988, while owning 100% shares of the company and controlling and managing the company, sold 49% shareholding of the company out of which 34% shareholding was sold to the public and 15% to the workers/employees; before the above sale of 49% shareholding, the company, on 10.10.1988, issued prospectus wherein Tk.  5,25,33,742.00, which is the appreciated value of the assets of the company after revaluation was shown as interest free quasi equity loan the company; in the balance Sheet for the years 1989-90 upto 1993-94 this quasi equity loan was also shown as interest free; after sale of 49% shareholding of the company, the appellant No. 1 also decided to dis-invest its balance 51% shares and accordingly by Public Notice dated 5.8.92 tenders were invited for sale of those 51 % shares and taking advantage of its majority shareholding in the company the appellant No. 1, prior to above sale of the remaining 51% shares, obtained Board Resolutions dated 25.4.94 in its 74th Board Meeting approving the decision to secure the above quasi equity loan of Tk. 5,25,33,742/- with interest o 13.5% by bank guarantee but in the 76th Board Meeting held on 19.6.94, the appellants by virtue of their greater voting power, got a resolution passed approving issuance of 5253 debentures of Tk. 10,000 each payable with interest @ 13.5% to secure repayment of the above quasi equity loan; further in the 77m extra ordinary general meeting of the company held on 27.6.94 the appellants, by virtue of their greeter voting power, got the decision to issue debentures with interest approved by the company and then 5253 debentures covering the quasi equity loan payment of Tk. 5,25,33,742.00 were issued in favour of the appellant No. 1 and 7776 debentures covering the loan of Tk. 6,77,73,372 due to the appellant No. 2 were issued in favour of the appellant No. 2; the appellants having sold their shares on 15.12,94 and having created the Deed of Trust just one day before for payment of their fictitious dues by virtue of the Board Resolution, have  perpetrated "fraud-on-minority" and besides, the resolutions contravened the mandatory provision of the Companies Act 1994 inasmuch as the interested directors voted without declaring their interest and further the said resolutions did not section payment of 13.5% interest perineum on both the quasi-equity and also the so called dues of the appellant No. 2 and so the said resolutions are no resolutions in the eye of law and moreover the said resolutions being detrimental to the interest of the company as well as the minority shareholders; are void. 

 7. The appellant No. 2 contested the above matter and filed affidavit-in-opposition contending that before sale of 49% of the company, the value of the assets of the company was revalued as since its initial incorporation, the value of the assets of the company had increased manifold and on revaluation of the land, building, machinery, equipments etc by the  Chartered Accountants as on 31.6.1988, Tk. 5,25,33,742.00 which was the appreciated value of the assets, was shown as quasi equity loan given by the appellant No. 1 to the company; since the value of the assets of the company increased manifold and the company was also a profitable concern, the actual value of the shares of the company also increased manifold but 49% shares were sold only at face value; as a result the shares offered were oversubscribed; in view of the above the purchasers of 49%. shares, i.e 2,45,000 shares, while purchasing shares, did not raise any objection to the creation of the above quasi equity loan and also purchased 49% shares without raising any objection;  subsequently the appellant No. 1 issued Public Notice for sale of its balance 51% shares, i.e 2,55,000 shares, to the public and in the Public Notice for the above sale it was specifically provided that the said quasi equity loan was made payable by the company to the appellant No. 1 with interest 13.5% and for payment of the same debentures will be created by the company to secure the above loan and the respondent No. 3, whose did being height was accepted, considering that the actual value of the assets were much more than the value as shown and the company was also a profitable concern, apart from agreeing that the company against the quasi equity loan will issue debentures with interest also purchased the 51 % shareholding, that is 2,55,000 shares, at U.S.$ 5,00,000/-, which is many times more than the face value; further when decision in respect of creation of quasi equity loan was taken in the meeting of the Board of Directors as well as in the extraordinary general meeting of the company, none raised any objection. 

 8. The High Court Division, after hearing the applications analogously, by common judgment, allowed the applications and cancelled the respective debentures as being void holding, amongst others, that (a) A member has an interest in maintaining the value of his share and he may bring himself within section 233 if he can show that the value of its shareholding is seriously diminished or jeopardized by reason of conduct of those having defect control of the company which is unfair to the member concerned. A member has an interest in competent management of a company, its profitability, dividend policy which will have effect on his financial interest as a shareholder and on the value of his shares. The act or omission by the majority who are in defector control of the company affecting the interest of the share-holders generally including the petitioners as a minority shareholder is called in question in an application under section 233. (b) A company and is shareholder are two distinct and separate entitles. A majority shareholder cannot appropriate to them-selves money, property or advantages which belong to the company or in which shareholders are entitled to participate. Such conduct amounts to fraud on minority and cannot be anticipating; such conduct amounts to fraud on minority and cannot be ratified. A malafide exercise of powers by Directors affecting interest of the company as well as shareholders generally is not rectifiable. If the company is deprived of its assets because of the majority approving such decision, it would be in itself is fraud on minority. (c) It is permissible if a shareholder allows the company to retain an amount of the profit payable to him by way of dividend as loan to the company to retain an amount of the profit payable to him by way of dividend as loan to the company. A surplus of assets over liabilities share capital and capital reserved is treated as distributable profit. Such a surplus includes profits. Such a surplus includes profits obtained on the sale of fixed assets for more than their cost price or written down value. A company is prevented from paying dividend out of profit unless current profit is sufficient to write off earlier losses. (d) There cannot be any profit out of revaluation of any fixed assets without disposal of the same by sale or otherwise and that too without writing off the treading losses of earlier financial years. (e) A shareholder does not become automatically entitled to any part of the profit until resolution is taken and a dividend is declared by the company out of such profit. (f) The prospectus stated that the quasi equity loan was created out of an estimated profit arising out of increased value of the assets over the years since incorporation of value of the assets over the years since incorporation of value of the assets, over the years since incorporation of the company by revaluating the assets without disposal of the same and without any resolution declaring the dividend from such profit and that too without deducting the accumulated loss of Tk. 546 crore as is 30.6.1988. Even the Auditors opined that earlier losses ought to have been deducted from the said quasi equity loan. (g) A shareholder cannot claim the increased amount in the value of any asset of the company without realising the same by disposal of the asset as it would offend the principles of company law. His interest confirm to by shareholding in the company. Appreciation of value of fixed asset is also a fixed capital of the company and such increase in the fixed capital enhances share value. Such increase cannot be considered profit. Therefore, the quasi equity loan in question is not tenable in law and is not repayable to GOB: (h) If the company is made to repay the quasi equity loan, it would amount to diminishing the value of the shares of the company which could prejudice the interest of the shareholders including the petitioners, and it would also affect the interest of the company. (i) It appeared from the minutes of AGM on 10.6.93 and EGM on 12.9.93 that the minority, opposed the creation of debenture and repayment of quasi equity loan, but majority voting power wrongfully created quasi equity loan and approved the same in the Board and General Meeting. The said quasi equity loan is harsh, burdensome and wrongful to the petitioners, minority shareholders and the Board and General Meeting resolutions are oppressive and prejudicial. 

 9. Leave has been granted to consider whether the High Court Division fell in error in not holding that a resolution passed by the majority in a duly convened meeting of the shareholders, with due notice of it, and passed after, full and thorough discussion could not be objected subsequently by some of the shareholders who were present in the said meeting and that in Matter of 6 of 1996 one of the shareholder, in the meeting made a statement that he had no objection to repayment of quasi equity loan as well as other dues of the appellants or to the issue of debentures but only that the interest on the debentures was not acceptable to him and the finding of the High Court Division is clearly against the deliberations in the said meeting and the said extra ordinary resolution dated 23.9.1993, on which the High Court Division relied was passed after the appellants had ceased to be the shareholders of the company and the respondent No.  49 in Civil Appeal No. 171 of 2000, the transferees of the 51% the shares of CCCG, collusively abstained in the voting and thereby allowing the passing of the said resolution in which it was held that the company was unfairly made to agree to the creation of the quasi equity loans and debentures by the appellants; further the said resolution also completely contradicted the proceeding of the 4th Annual General Meeting of the Company held on 23.6.93 and further allowing the application under section 233 of the Companies Act 1994 in which the company itself is a petitioner is not permissible; the High Court Division, fell in error in not addressing itself to the objection of the appellants as to the maintainability of the petition on the ground that the respondents in the respective matters did not hold 10%. the issued shares which is a prerequisite for the locus standi to file the applications under above section 233 of the Companies Act 1994; the High Court Division erroneously ordered cancellation of the quasi equity loans and the debentures inasmuch as the same have been shown in the prospectus issued for sale of 49% sharers of the above companies and further all the audited balance sheets of the companies since creation of the quasi equity loans and debentures were also approved by the Board of Directors of the companies and also the shareholders in the successive extra ordinary and annual general meetings of the companies; since the audited balance sheet remained legal, valid and binding on the companies and its share-holders those quasi judicial loans and the consequent debentures could not be cancelled; the High Court Division also fell in error in holding that revaluation of the fixed assets were profits which can only be given to a shareholder upon declaration of dividend after adjusting its earlier losses and that there is no rule or principle or provision of law making revaluation of fixed assets as profits of the company and so the same was a fraud on the minority without considering that at the time of creation of the quasi equity loan, the appellants were 100% shareholders of the companies and there was no minority share-holding in the companies at that time; further filing of civil cases is not a bar the present application's under section 233 of the Companies Act. 1994. 

 10. Mr. Shafique Ahmed, the learned counsel for the appellants in Civil Appeal Nos. 171-173 of 2000, submitted that the High Court Division fell in, error in not considering that in all the appeals, long before 49% sharps were  dis-invested, revaluations of the assets of the respective companies were made and quasi equity loans were created in respect of the appreciated value at a time when the appellants were the owners of the 100% shareholding of the respective companies and the appellants sold 49% shareholding subsequently and there being no minority shares at the time of creation of the above quasi equity loans, the question of committing fraud upon the minority shareholders including the respondents did not arise; the purchasers of 49% shares i.e the minority shareholders including the respondents, before subscribing to the shares, in view of the disclosures made in the prospectus, were well aware that the of quasi equity loans were the appreciated value of the assets of the respective companies but without raising any objection to the creations of the above quasi equity loans they purchased the shares on consideration that the value of the assets of the companies having increased manifold and the companies were also profitable concerns, the actual value of the shares were also many times more than the face value but the said 49% shareholding were being sold at face value and further the appellant No. 1, on consideration that the companies would remain under its management till sale of balance 51 % shareholding, did not realize the amounts of appreciated value and allowed the companies to retain the amounts as quasi equity loans and also did not demand any interest on the said loan but that does not mean that those quasi equity loans would remain interest free and at the time of sale of the balance 51% shares in the Public Notice, claimed interest @ 13.5%; further the said quasi equity loans having been shown in all the audited balance sheets of the companies since their creations and those being passed and approved in the respective meetings of the Board of Directors as well as extraordinary general meetings of the respective companies duly convened with due notice of it and passed after thorough discussion, could not be objected subsequently by some of the shareholders and so the debentures issued against those quasi equity loans remained legally valid and finding on the companies as well as their shareholders; further the balance sheets; certified by the auditors and approved by the shareholders, are the only documents reflecting the assets and liabilities of a company and so those cannot be challenged in the proceeding in question and accordingly the applications under section 233 are barred by the principles of limitation, estoppel, waiver and acquiescence; moreover in respect of Matter No. 6 of 1996, as it will appear from the minutes of the extraordinary general meeting of CCCG held on 10.6.93, the petitioner No. 3 in the above matter, the respondent No. 3 herein, representing the minority shareholding, made a statement in the said meeting to the effect that he had no objection to the repayment of quasi equity loan and other dues of the appellant No. 1 or to the issue of debentures but merely the interest on debenture was not acceptable and so the objection raised in the said meeting was in respect of interest only; further, the resolution dated 23.9.93 on which the High Court relied, was taken in the extra ordinary general meetings after the appellants of the Matter No. 46 of 1996 ceased to be the shareholders of the company and their successor, the respondent No. 49, though at the time of subscribing 51 % shareholding and also in the Agreement for Sale dated 27.6.1993 agreed that the company will issue debentures with interest, collusively abstained from casting vote in that meeting and thereby allowed passing of the said resolution; further the said resolution also contradicted the contents of the proceeding of the 4th annual general meeting held on 10,6.1993; further in the above matter the company itself being the petitioner No. 5, the application under section 233 is also not maintainable and further the High Court Division fell in error in deciding the issues involved in this matter which involved question of facts and a civil suit filed by the respondents in respect of self-same issues is also pending. 

 11. Mr. Syed Amirul Islam, the learned counsel for the respondents Nos.  6 and 7 in Civil Appeal No.  171 of 2000, submitted that the majority cannot commit a fraud on minority by converting and appropriating to itself properties of the company even by convening a meeting which is procedurally valid inasmuch as the law of fraud on minority does not revolve around the legality of the procedure and section 233 of the Companies Act. 1994 contemplates that if it is brought to the notice of the Court that the affairs of the Company are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to the interest of a member then the Court can grant relief and hence it is immaterial that the petitioner No. 3 of Matter No. 6 of 1996 had accepted the motion of a quasi equity loan but objected to it only in respect of interest and further the Court has power to act even if the resolution dated 21.8.93 adopted in the extraordinary general meeting of the company but was ineffective however the resolution passed in that meeting would show the rejection of the quasi equity loan by the minority shareholders of the company; the annual general meeting held on 10.6.1993 cannot give validity to a transaction effectively allowing payment out of capital in the garb of quasi equity loan in as much as even if all the shareholders agree, the appellants cannot expropriate to themselves personally the assets of the company without following the legal procedure of either declaring a dividend on profits or redemption of share capital where redeemable shares are issued or reduction of capital after following the procedures as laid down in company law in this regard and further even if an entry is wrongly recorded in the balance sheet and was not objected by anyone that will also not give validity to a transaction which would essentially amount to payment out of capital by reducing the assets without following the legal procedures for such reduction of capital and that the concept of such quasi equity loan is unknown in Company law and further the balance sheets of the company for the years ending 30.06.90 and 30.06.91 will show that the alleged quasi-equity loan was interest free and as such even if the said loan was valid, the interest charged thereon and the issuance of the debenture of Tk. 13,79,06,705.00 with interest at the rate of 13.5% was nothing but a fraud on the minority shareholders and further even if the net asset value of the company had appreciated, it became the asset of the company and not of the appellants and as such the creation of the quasi equity loan through conversion of the appreciated asset of the company was expropriation of the asset of the company and hence a fraud on minority. 

 12. Mr. Azmalul Hossain, QC, representing the respondent Nos. 1-5 in Civil Appeal No. 172 of 2000 submitted that the quasi-equity loan being an asset of the company belongs to the company and not to any particular member or any group of members and the company is entirely distinct from its members and as held in Burland v Earle (1902) AC 83 the majority shareholders cannot appropriate to themselves money, property or advantages that belong to the company or in which other shareholders are entitled to participate and it thus follows that the quasi equity loan, being part of the assets of the company, does not belong to the appellants, the majority shareholders any more than it belongs to the minority shareholders and therefore the appellants are not entitled in law to appropriate the increased value of the assets of the company at all and the quasi equity loan, being revaluation of assets, is not money that can be taken out of the company and only when assets are sold then only the sale proceed can be taken out of the company more so when it is a simple book entry; further after paying the consideration for the shares, the 49% and 51% shareholders having already paid for the quasi equity loan there is no further scope for them for payment thereafter; the respective prospectus and schedule 3 to the agreement for the sale of 51% shares show that the revaluation of the assets of the company, the quasi equity loan, is part of its net worth and therefore, both the purchasers of 49% sharers as well as 51% sharers have already paid for the net worth when they paid the purchase price for the shares to the appellants and if the appellants are allowed to enforce the debentures, it would amount to receiving payment for the assets of the company twice, once for the shares and secondly for the debentures; and thus the acts of the appellants tantamount to expropriation of the assets of the company for their interest and it cannot be said to be an act which is in the interests of the company and thus the actions of the appellants are ultra vires the Memorandum and Articles and malafide and accordingly as held in (Cook v Decks (1916) 1 AC 554) such acts cannot also be ratified even at an extra ordinary general meeting of the company; moreover the decisions taken at the meeting of the Board of Directors in its 58th meeting is also invalid in law as the interested directors, being the nominees of the appellants, voted thereon and passed the resolutions to secure the of quasi equity loan by the issue of debentures and this is not permissible under the provisions of sections 130 and 131 of the Companies Act 1994 and also in terms of the principles as laid down in Smith v Fawcett (1942) Ch,304; Colin Gwyer & Associates Ltd v London Wharf (Lime house) Ltd and Eaton Bray v Palmer (2002) EWHC 2748; Charterbridge Corporation Ltd. v Lloyds Bank Ltd (1970) Ch.62; Md. Yameen v Bashar 1986 I3LD(AD)305); the resolution dated 10.6.1993 passed in the extraordinary general meeting is invalid as no vote was taken regarding the quasi equity loan to be converted into secured/redeemable debentures with interest @ 13.50%; moreover only profits of any company properly defined may be taken out as dividends and the quasi equity loan cannot be said to be the profits of the company as held in Wood v Odessa Waterworks Co (1889)42 Ch.D.636; Burland v Earle (1902) AC 83; Lee v Neuchatel Asphalte Co (1889)41 Ch.D.1; Dovey v Cory (1901) AC 477; though in the balance sheet the quasi equity loan was shown but as held in Daniels v Daniels (1978) 1 Ch.406; the same having been prepared and approved by the nominees of the appellants cannot help the appellants to establish an acknowledgment on the part of the company or the minority shareholders; the pendency of the civil suit is also irrelevant for the purposes of deciding the matters in as much under section 233 of the Companies Act 1994 the High Court Division has exclusive jurisdiction to deal with the issues raised in the applications in question and those issues cannot be decided in the civil suit and therefore and accordingly the High Court Division was right to ignore the civil suits and further, there is nothing in section 233 which places a bar to remedy as sought in the present matters.

It thus appears that the purchasers of 49% shareholding, including the respondents of the respective appeals, being not shareholders of the respective companies at the time of creation of the quasi equity loans, the question of keeping them in the dark and/or misleading/misinforming that as to the creation of quasi equity loan and also committing fraud upon minority does not arise and further the purchases of 49% shareholders of the companies including the respondents even knowing about the quasi equity loans as shown in the respective prospectus, in order to make huge gain, subscribed the shares without raising any objection to the creation of quasi equity loans and in fact the above shares were oversubscribed; further after about. 4 years, the purchasers of 51% shareholding, apart from acknowledging the liability of the companies to issue debentures with 13.5% interest against the above quasi equity loans, purchased the shares at a price which is many times more than the face value at which the purchasers of 49% shareholding, including the respondents, purchased the shares.
